themes_detail.label: Street Conditions Deteriorating Rapidly
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints in CD 205 spiked to 19 THIS WEEK, a 230% increase from the 5.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.94), suggesting rapid pavement degradation or pothole formation in Fordham/University Heights.
evidence: 19 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.8 weekly baseline (230% spike, z-score 4.94)
Concurrent spike in illegal dumping complaints: 15 THIS WEEK vs. 4.4 avg (243% increase, z-score 4.02)
Community Board budget requests for increased sanitation equipment suggest chronic street maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Survey street conditions in high-complaint blocks; identify whether winter damage or ongoing neglect is the cause
Connect street deterioration to illegal dumping spike—are potholes and debris linked to sanitation service gaps?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Exploding
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints in CD 205 skyrocketed to 15 LAST WEEK, a 900% increase from the 1.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.55, highest severity), indicating a rapid expansion of homelessness or informal settlements.
evidence: 15 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (900% spike, z-score 9.55—highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Concurrent spike in 'outside building' complaints: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 avg (500% increase, z-score 5.0)
Community Board requests for public health programs suggest unmet needs in homeless services or shelter capacity
reporting_angles: Locate the encampments (parks, sidewalks, subway areas) and interview residents about conditions and needs
Report on whether city services are responding; connect to housing crisis and shelter capacity in the Bronx

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped to 10 LAST WEEK, a 281% increase from the 2.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.69), signaling potential HVAC failures, mold, or ventilation issues across residential buildings.
evidence: 10 indoor air quality complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly baseline (281% spike, z-score 3.69)
Heat/hot water remains the highest volume complaint category (7,530 over 90 days), suggesting systemic building maintenance failures
Community Board has outstanding air quality investigation request to DEP, indicating prior unresolved concerns
reporting_angles: Investigate whether the spike is driven by heating season failures or mold in specific buildings; file FOIL request for air quality test results
Interview residents about respiratory symptoms and building conditions; connect to broader housing quality issues

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints in CD 205 reached 15 THIS WEEK, a 243% increase from the 4.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.02), paired with street condition spikes, suggesting environmental neglect and sanitation service gaps.
evidence: 15 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.4 weekly average (243% increase, z-score 4.02)
Synchronized spike in street sweeping complaints: 5 LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 avg (400% increase, z-score 4.62)
Community Board repeated budget requests for additional sanitation trucks/equipment indicate chronic understaffing
reporting_angles: Map dumping hotspots; interview residents and Sanitation Department about service frequency and enforcement
Investigate whether reduced street sweeping capacity is enabling illegal dumping

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage / Environmental Stress
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints in CD 205 rose to 3 LAST WEEK, a 1,100% increase from the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35), likely tied to recent winter weather but worth monitoring for broader canopy health issues.
evidence: 3 damaged tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1,100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Prior snow/ice complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 149 vs. 20.0 avg (645% increase), explaining recent tree damage
Community Board budget request for DPR capital projects suggests ongoing park and tree maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks to assess winter damage to urban forest; verify whether tree inventory/maintenance is adequate
Quick visual survey of major parks in Fordham/University Heights to document visible damage
